attempts.summary: Removed the injected WB_FaultScan watchdog that forced running:=TRUE at scan 24, which caused P_STOP/P_INTERLOCK violations. Core logic preserved: rising-edge start latch, stop/permit dominance, prevStart updated every scan (R3).

final_evaluation.sampling: Fresh FB per scenario; all inputs assigned each scan; outputs observed after invocation. Times and TIME/LTIME interface values are milliseconds. First eligible TON invocation has elapsed=0. No real-time/hardware claim.

reviews.summary: The implementation matches R1-R3: previous-start edge memory is updated before blocking logic on every scan, stop/permit blocking dominates simultaneous start edges, and held start cannot restart after unblocking. No semantic discrepancy found.

findings.name: startup_rising_edge_latches
findings.basis: R1: running latches TRUE only on a rising edge of start while permit is TRUE and stop is FALSE; previous start is FALSE at startup.

findings.name: stop_dominates_simultaneous_start_edge
findings.basis: R2: stop TRUE immediately clears running and dominates a simultaneous start rising edge.

findings.name: permit_false_blocks_and_held_start_no_restart
findings.basis: R3: start edge memory updates during blocked scans, so restoring permit while start remains held does not restart; R2: permit FALSE clears running.

findings.name: stop_blocked_held_start_no_restart
findings.basis: R2: stop TRUE clears running; R3: edge memory updates during blocked scans, so releasing stop while start remains held does not restart.
